pdfium_measurement.comparison: At x=164,y=95..110 the negative renders gray 252-253 while matched control renders 254-255. All 16 line pixels remain 1-3 gray levels darker than control; mean modified-source pixel is 250.125 versus original local source background mean 254.8125 (contrast 4.6875), and mean final contrast versus matched PDFium control is 1.75 (37.3% of source contrast). The mark remains measurable but is materially weakened by full-page reduced-background/JPEG representation.
pdfium_measurement.interpretation: The line lies outside the glyph-mask one-pixel fringe loop (the owned crop ends at x=162), so this exact x=164 test does not exercise the classifier predicate. It demonstrates no full deletion by the classifier but exposes a background-layer fidelity weakness: unknown one-pixel low-contrast content receives no native-resolution patch and loses about 63% of its local contrast. A classifier-specific unowned-mark test must put a mark within a candidate fringe pixel while keeping it out of ownership; a mark with exactly donor-predicted grayscale coverage is intrinsically indistinguishable from genuine antialiasing from source intensities alone.

latest_review.projection_review: No concrete projection or indexing defect found. Gray halo indexing is checked against crop+4 bounds; selected sibling witness grayscale is retained in document.rs before visual dictionary prototype handling.

review_findings.finding: Sibling grayscale evidence is retained correctly: document.rs clones each selected bounded donor and calls retain_grayscale before prefixing/adding it. __doc_donor prototypes skip threshold refinement but retain the preattached gray samples and 2px halo.

The isolated unowned low-contrast line at x=164,y=95..110 is not erased by the vector-fringe classifier (it lies outside the accepted a mask and its one-pixel loop), but the full-page reduced background/JPEG layer weakens its local contrast from 4.6875 gray levels in source to 1.75 in PDFium relative to the matched control: about 37.3% retained. This is a concrete preservation risk for subthreshold unknown content that never becomes a native-resolution patch.

The classifier’s per-pixel donor-intensity test cannot distinguish an unrelated mark from antialiasing if the mark lands within its fringe footprint and exactly matches predicted donor coverage. A hard-negative unit test at an actual candidate fringe pixel is needed to expose/document this irreducible ambiguity; the x=164 line test does not trigger that condition.

ordinary_negative.result: All 16 pixels remain visible. Against the matched output control, mean local contrast is 4.4375 gray levels versus 4.6875 in source (94.7% retained); one naturally 252 source sample becomes 251, so no attenuation regression is observed for this target line.
ordinary_negative.limitation: The latest guard is a bounded heuristic, not a guarantee for arbitrary unknown content: the source comment/code require source-vs-background dark residual >=2, horizontal/vertical ridge contrast >=3 against +/-2px neighbours, and run length >=8. Diagonal marks, runs shorter than 8, contrast below thresholds, or marks merged with protected/suppressed pixels have no general preservation guarantee. The earlier x=164 line is preserved by the coherent residual path; it is not proof for every faint mark.

implementation_review.finding: The in-bounds glyph-neighborhood, residual and explicit protected patches use source pixel coordinates and are composed above the reduced background. The line tests found no projection/indexing defect for in-bounds source coordinates.
implementation_review.risk: The 32px tile ridge test resets run length at each tile boundary, so an axis-aligned coherent segment crossing a tile boundary can be split into two sub-8 runs and miss this residual guard. The separate glyph-neighborhood and explicit protected guards cover only their footprints. protected patches currently preserve their bbox rectangle, not polygon-exact shape, which is conservative for content but can cost more.

implementation_review.safe_fix: Iterate already clamped, nonempty protected_boxes for unconditional raster patches, preserving one-to-one region mapping if IDs are needed; otherwise clamp and filter each polygon bbox before patch_from_rgb.
implementation_review.current_residual_seam_finding: The seam-corrected implementation detects the full continuous ridge before assigning 32px storage cells. The saved crossing-seam regression now passes. In the ordinary negative, native patch resource /Im3 stores x164,y95=250 exactly; PDFium renders 252 at that pixel, indicating a residual renderer/placement discrepancy rather than an unowned sample.
